sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Wholesale Brokerage of Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; French-inspired Companies Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; EU directives transposed directly; no sub-state tax distinctions)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income and Capital Tax Convention (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–Germany Tax Treaty (2012, as aligned by the OECD Multilateral Instrument)
Luxembourg–China (PRC) DTA of 1994, with amending Protocol signed in 2019 (subject to ratification)
Luxembourg–Netherlands DTA of 1968, as amended by the 1990 and 1999 Protocols
Energy Charter Treaty (in force for Luxembourg since 16 April 1998)
EU–Singapore Free Trade Agreement (in force 21 November 2019)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI), ratified by Luxembourg with entry into force during 2021

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); UBO Register: Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as amended by the Law of 28 July 2020 and the Law of 14 December 2021; RCS: Law of 19 December 2002 on the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés; Sectoral AML guidance: CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 and CSSF Circular 18/681; FIU: Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF); FATF Recommendations as implemented by Luxembourg.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access restricted following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022; the RBE is available to Luxembourg authorities, the CRF, and obliged entities with a demonstrated legitimate interest; companies must file UBO data within one month of incorporation and maintain the UBO file at the registered office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Registration Extract (Extrait du registre) of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or Chamber of Commerce of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (certificat de non-faillite or equivalent long-form extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry, notary or tax authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized General Power of Attorney granted to the Luxembourg notary and designated incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified notary in the signatory's country (or the Luxembourg notary where signature occurs in the Grand Duchy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport/ID copies and proof of residential address for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority, local notary or sworn translator in the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification of true copy; Hague Apostille preferred (Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO declaration with corporate structure chart (owner organigram) identifying each natural person controlling the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner, or legal counsel acting for the shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention countries)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and principal counterparties against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Luxembourg CRF/FIU lists and CSSF Circular 18/681 guidance; additional PEP identification per FATF Recommendation 12; enhanced due diligence on all non-EU corporate investors and on fuel-trading counterparties; initial verification at formation, re-screening upon control changes and before each material transaction; AML records retained for five years after termination of the business relationship (Article 45 of the AML Law).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), official portal https://www.lbr.lu (e-filing via espace.lbr.lu); public name-availability search via the RCS query interface.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filings are made in French; the articles of association and registration abstracts must be in French, while the corporate name itself may use Latin-script characters of any EU language. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet with a French or German phonetic transcription. The name must be distinctive, lawful and non-misleading, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-registered name or a protected trademark or trade name in Luxembourg.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (prior CSSF authorization under the Law of 5 April 1993)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
SICAV / SICAF / Fonds d'investissement / UCITS / AIF (prior CSSF authorization under the Law of 17 December 2010)
Fiduciaire / Trust / Gestion de Fortune (regulated-activity tokens requiring prior ministerial authorization)

Pétrole / Pétrolier / Petroleum / Crude Oil / Fuel (sector-sensitive tokens requiring evidence of the applicable Ministry of the Economy establishment authorization or fuel-products license to avoid a misleading holding-out)
Luxembourg / Grand-Duché / État / Ministère / Université / Chambre de Commerce (institutional or official-sounding tokens allowed only with prior approval of the competent state body)
Marine / Shipping / Commodity Broker (may trigger an additional regulation check under the Law of 2 September 2011 on establishment authorization for the wholesale fuel-brokerage activity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a formal stand-alone name-reservation register; the notary performs an RCS availability check at the moment of deed preparation and the name is captured in the draft articles. In case of refusal, the notary first requests an informal re-examination; if the RCS registrar maintains the refusal, an appeal lies to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 40 days of the written refusal, attaching the draft articles and a negative name-search certificate. Alternatively, the applicant submits a corrected name set, which restarts the 30-day window; reserving two or three alternative names with the notary is the established market practice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not_Acceptable_For_Target_Industry — a correspondence-only or virtual-address arrangement is insufficient for a high-risk physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates; the SARL must maintain a genuine Luxembourg principal place of business with dedicated office facilities, locally accessible books and records, a locally resident director (or equivalent substance delegation), and a Luxembourg bank account with ongoing local KYC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 18% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months, rising to 30–35% where annual turnover exceeds EUR 10,000,000; on-site controls may be conducted by the CRF (FIU), the Ministry of the Economy under the establishment-authorization regime, and the VAT administration (AEDT), under Article 17 of the AML Law and Article 22 of the Law of 2 September 2011.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 19 December 2016; Book X – Société à Responsabilité Limitée, Articles 710-1 to 710-26; Law of 10 June 1999 establishing the Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarized incorporation deed) together with application for registration in the RCS (formulaire de demande d'inscription).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital is EUR 1.00. The entire subscribed capital must be fully subscribed and at least 25% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation. The paid-up amount must be deposited in a blocked escrow account ('dépôt bloqué') at a Luxembourg credit institution until RCS registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation of the Company under the proposed corporate name, to be confirmed in the Articles of Association, is hereby authorized and approved. That the full share capital as set out in the draft Articles shall be subscribed by the incorporators and the initial paid-up portion lodged in a blocked account at a Luxembourg bank. That the registered office shall be established at the address stated in the Articles within Luxembourg City. That the Manager named therein is appointed as Gérant with sole and full authority to execute the notarial deed, open bank accounts, and undertake all filings and publications required for the acquisition of legal personality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a CSSF-licensed bank. Provide the draft Articles of Association and KYC documents. Instruct the bank to open a blocked account in the intended name of the company. Transfer at least 25% of the subscribed cash share capital into the account. Obtain the bank's blocked account certificate evidencing the balance.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Passport and proof of address of each shareholder
Declaration of beneficial ownership
Bank account opening form and application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC/AML queries, provide supplementary sworn statements or mission letters; alternatively, switch to another CSSF-licensed bank after securing pre-clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a meeting of all incorporators. The notary reads and verifies the draft Articles, confirms compliance with the law, receives the blocked bank certificate and other required dossiers. The incorporators sign the incorporation deed ('acte constitutif') and the manager formally accepts their appointment.
required_dossiers: Final draft Articles of Association
Blocked bank certificate
Passport copies of all incorporators
Powers of attorney for any represented shareholder
Proof of lawful registered office availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, revise the Articles and reconvene for a new signing; the deed may be amended by an additional notarial instrument without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated notarial deed (or its certified copy) to the RCS, together with the registration application form and specimen signatures of the appointed managers. The LBR reviews formal conformity and, upon acceptance, registers the company and allocates a RCS number.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed (original or certified extract)
RCS registration application form
Specimen signatures of managers
List of shareholders and the number of shares held
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond with supplementary documentation or a corrective filing within one month. Failure to cure requires a fresh filing and an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the standard tax registration form ('formulaire de constitution d'un dossier') with the AEDT, citing the newly issued RCS number. Upon processing, the company obtains a VAT identification number and is enrolled for corporate income tax and municipal business tax purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extract)
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Identity documents of managers and shareholders
Lease or proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed, contact the AEDT's central dossier office; tax numbers are issued retroactively to the incorporation date once KYC is verified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economy – Department of Energy (Direction de l'énergie)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a petroleum products trading licence ('licence de négoce de produits pétroliers') under the Law of 12 December 1996 on the electricity and gas market, as amended, and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 1998 concerning the marketing and sale of petroleum products. Include proof of RCS registration, financial standing, corporate AML/CTF policies, and the appointment of a compliance officer.
required_dossiers: Application form for petroleum products trading licence
RCS extract (less than 3 months old)
Articles of Association including statutory purpose
Financial statements or proof of capitalization
AML/CTF policy manual and compliance officer appointment
KYC documentation for shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of refusal or protracted examination, the applicant may submit a reasoned appeal to the Minister of Economy within one month of the notification of refusal; alternatively, augment the file with a dedicated compliance officer and external AML audit to secure approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – Department of Energy (Direction de l'énergie)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de négoce de produits pétroliers (Petroleum Products Wholesale Trading Licence)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category D (tertiary office-based brokerage; no installation classée under the Law of 21 December 1999 on environmental permits). If physical storage or handling is added in the future, a full EIA will be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure brokerage operations. Any incidental fuel handling must comply with VOC emission limits (VOC concentration ≤ 150 mg C/Nm³) set out in the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 March 2004 implementing Directive 2010/75/EU, and must ensure no soil or water contamination under the Law of 21 December 1999 on water management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificat de sécurité incendie) is required for the registered office if the premises exceed 200 persons' capacity or 500 m² usable floor area; this is issued by the Inspection Générale de la Protection Civile after inspection. Occupational clearance from the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) is mandatory, including the declaration of any employees and compliance with the Luxembourg Labor Code (travaux réglementés, first-aid, and workplace risk assessment).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg; direct tax authority: Administration des contributions (ACD); official e-filing portal: MyGuichet.lu / eTVA
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Luxembourg must register for VAT via the AEDT before carrying out taxable supplies in the Grand Duchy. The application is submitted electronically through MyGuichet.lu or via AEDT Form 100 (TVA); non-EU/third-country entities must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative established in Luxembourg unless an exemption applies under a VAT mutual assistance agreement. The AEDT issues a 15-digit national VAT identification number (format LU + 8-digit). For corporate income tax, the entity must first be registered in the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and obtain a Luxembourg business number; corporate tax registration is then effected with the Administration des contributions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a check-the-box mechanism. Available elections include (i) group taxation (fiscal unity) for resident companies with 95% owned taxable persons under Article 164ter of the Income Tax Law (LIR); (ii) participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains under Article 166 LIR; (iii) hybrid mismatch and subject-to-tax elections under the ATAD implementation law (loi du 18 décembre 2019); (iv) optional simplified VAT small-enterprise exemption regime under Article 57 of the VAT Law (loi TVA).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 of annual taxable turnover for resident small businesses; no threshold for non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg; EUR 10,000 for intra-Community distance sales to Luxembourg consumers
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for business-to-government (B2G) transactions through the PEPPOL network (BIS 3.0); no statutory B2B e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance; VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (monthly or quarterly based on turnover); no digital stamping or continuous transaction controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically exported outside the European Union qualify for 0% VAT where the supplier retains documentation proving the export within 30 days (or an extended period approved by the AEDT). Intra-EU dispatches of goods to a customer identified by a valid EU VAT number are zero-rated if the EC sales list is submitted. Additionally, supplies of marine fuel and lubricants to ships operated for international navigation (bunker fuels) are exempt with a right to deduction under Article 50 of the VAT Law, subject to proof of the ship's international voyage.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retroactively recharacterise zero-rated exports as domestic taxable supplies if the required documentary evidence is not held at the time of dispatch. The resulting assessment is at 17% VAT, plus monthly late interest of 0.6% and administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000 for documentation failures. Fraudulent export-zero-rating claims are subject to criminal sanctions under Article 92 of the VAT Law (imprisonment of up to three years and/or a fine of up to EUR 250,000), together with a retrospective clawback for five years and the loss of the right to automatic VAT refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); prudential conduct supervision and AML/CTF oversight of banks are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector and the Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies no exchange control restrictions. The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account, consistent with Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-65 and the euro-area freedoms. Profit repatriation, dividend distributions, interest, royalties, repayment of shareholder loans and liquidation proceeds are unrestricted, provided corporate law formalities are met (annual general meeting approval of distributions, statutory auditor statement when required under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, and the net-asset test). Practical hurdles are limited to (i) banking due-diligence documentation, (ii) EU/OFAC and United Nations sanctions screening on counterparties and payment corridors, and (iii) the absence of a correspondent relationship for banks located in non-cooperative or high-risk jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements and no minimum mandatory conversion ratios in Luxembourg. A Luxembourg entity engaged in the physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates may freely retain foreign currency receipts in a Luxembourg bank account, convert them at market rates, or apply them to offshore trade settlement. The only obligations are general AML/CFT record-keeping and accounting transparency under CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, and the Luxembourg Commercial Code; no BCL declaration or license is required for foreign currency holdings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Trade Finance and LC Settlement Account
Operational Account; Commodity Trade Finance Account
Operational Account; Foreign Currency Account (USD multi-currency)
Operational Account; Standby LC and Guarantee Account
Operational Account; CNY and cross-border RMB Settlement Niche

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary collection/disbursement floats, Low for primary trade settlement. A Luxembourg or EEA-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Payment Institution, operating under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2), can provide IBAN accounts, FX conversion and payment initiation; however, wholesale marine-fuel brokerage transactions are high-value, high-volume and inherently risky, so major commodity counterparties, LC issuing banks and trade-finance providers will require settlement through a fully licensed credit institution with direct TARGET2 or SWIFT access. Non-EEA offshore digital EMIs (e.g., unregulated or weakly regulated entities in the Caribbean, Middle East or Asia) are not viable because (i) they lack access to SEPA/T2 and CHIPS/Fedwire, (ii) Luxembourg banks will reject incoming credits from unregulated EMI accounts as a de-risking measure, and (iii) documentary LC and standby LC rails cannot be operated through an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a statutory obligation for directors to appear physically at a bank branch; however, CSSF Regulation 12-02 (as amended), the AML Law of 12 November 2004, and CSSF Circular LCSD 17/683 require full identification and verification of the client, its senior managers and its beneficial owners. In practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one in-person or secured video-interview with the managing director, the ultimate beneficial owner(s) and the designated compliance officer; remote onboarding is permissible on a risk-based basis only for regulated or listed parent groups with robust digital identity verification (eIDAS qualified electronic signatures are accepted). For a newly formed SARL in the high-risk ISIC 4661 energy brokerage sector, expect physical presence at the bank premises or at a Luxembourg notary, along with certified corporate excerpts (RCS Luxembourg), apostilled and sworn-translated constitutional documents, sanctions screening, and signatory specimen signature formalities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: De novo SARL with no audited financial track record and high-risk energy commodity trading scope (ISIC 4661)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified business plan, pro-forma treasury forecast, share capital proof, list of strategic suppliers and buyers, due diligence files on counterparties, management CVs, internal AML/KYC and sanctions screening policies, and audited financial statements of the direct parent or guarantor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque intermediate holding chain involving offshore or low-transparency jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart identifying all ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) through the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), corporate registry extracts of each intermediate entity, notarised declarations, commercial rationale memorandum, confirmation that each intermediate vehicle is audited or regulated, and written background on the source of the initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from countries subject to sanctions, FATF grey lists, or high-risk third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening results (UN, EU, OFAC, UK), Know Your Counterparty (KYC) files, sanctions-licence opinions, Incoterms-linked trade contracts, bills of lading, certificates of origin, vessel vetting reports, and end-user/end-use certificates proving legitimate marine fuel logistics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material mismatch between declared equity capital and the size of proposed wire transfers or trade obligations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan agreements, subordination letters, bank-committed commodity trade finance facilities, Standby LC or documentary LC framework agreements, cash-flow projections showing trade cycle timing, and explanations of the difference between gross brokerage flows and net margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) among shareholders, directors or material counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit PEP designation, source of wealth and source of funds documentation (notarial certificates, tax returns, audited financials, share-sale deeds), enhanced monitoring plan, senior management approval in the credit file, and ongoing transaction monitoring reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of economic substance in Luxembourg, creating tax or money-laundering substance concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS corporate extract, lease agreement for Luxembourg registered offices with meeting rooms, employment contracts for resident trading/compliance staff, CSSF or ACL register evidence if applicable, Luxembourg VAT and CIT filings, board minutes on trading risk, and proof of local bank account administration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity injections and shareholder loans must be routed through the Luxembourg treasury account via TARGET2/SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR (SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008) with reference to the purpose code 'EQUI' (equity or participation) and the legal text 'Capital contribution to LU_SARL'; for USD/GBP/CHF injections use SWIFT MT103 through correspondent banks in New York or London, with the same purpose coding and full supporting remittance information. The bank will require the executed shareholder subscription resolutions, up-to-date register of shareholders, notarised deed of contribution (for in-kind or mixed contributions) and, where required, an independent auditor's report under the Law of 10 August 1915. The SARL statutory minimum capital threshold (EUR 12,000) must be fully paid or covered by a bank certificate; surplus injections can be booked as share premium or subordinated shareholder loans. All inbound USD received on the foreign-currency account may be converted to EUR or retained freely, subject only to the bank's pre-transaction sanctions and source-of-funds screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Physical commodity disbursements should be settled through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for direct freight, VAT, storage and demurrage payments; MT202 COV for third-party cover payments routed through correspondent banks; for price risk and documentary security, use MT700 (issued or confirmed commercial documentary LC), MT760 (standby LC) and, where appropriate, the SWIFT Trade Services Utility Bank Payment Obligation (BPO). USD settlement flows through CHIPS/Fedwire correspondents in New York; EUR flows clear in T2. Every payment instruction must be fully audit-trailed with the trade contract, commercial invoice, bill of lading, full set of shipping documents, independent inspection certificates (e.g., SGS, Intertek), quantity/quality reports, certificate of origin and customs declarations; instruction narrative should include purpose code 'TRAD' (Trade) or 'SUPP' (Suppliers), invoice/LC reference, and no inconsistent free-text. Payment release should be subject to a two-person authorisation matrix and real-time sanctions screening (OFAC, EU, UN) on all parties and vessels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) executed bilaterally with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution or investment firm under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, or under a 1998 FX Global Code-aligned master agreement, with physical delivery at maturity.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for hedging real trade receivables/payables denominated in non-convertible or restricted currencies of petroleum-importing jurisdictions; the NDF must be documented as a risk-reduction instrument tied to a specific underlying trade invoice.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) allowable for medium-term risk mitigation on trade-finance and working-capital facilities, subject to ISDA/CSA documentation, EMIR margin and reporting obligations (EU Regulation 648/2012), and internal hedge-policy approval.

Vanilla FX options (call/put, European style) are permissible for hedging commodity margin exposure where the hedging intent is documented under IFRS 9 hedge accounting; exotic or leveraged options are discouraged and generally unavailable absent a strong credit rating and additional collateral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of shareholders approving the annual accounts (Assemblée générale annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate body; signed minutes retained at the registered office, no RCS filing required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the AGM is not convened, the Public Prosecutor's Office or any interested party may petition the competent court to order the meeting; failure to approve annual accounts delays statutory filing, exposes the gérant to civil liability and permits the ACD to make an estimated tax assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing and publication (Comptes annuels) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBR e-file or MyGuichet.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end and not later than 1 month after AGM approval; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an LBR formal notice and administrative fines up to €1,000 per omission; persistent default is notified to the Public Prosecutor, who may petition the court for the judicial dissolution and strike-off of the SARL from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax (IRC) and municipal business tax (ICC) annual tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the following assessment year for calendar-year taxpayers (paper or e-filing via MyGuichet); ACD extensions may be requested, normally allowing filing until 31 December of that year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing warnings and coercion fines up to €25,000 under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung); late-payment interest at 0.6% per month on IRC/ICC due; if no return is filed, the ACD proceeds by estimated assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minimum net wealth tax (IF) return and annual payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg direct tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual cycle as the IRC return: filed and paid by 31 May for calendar-year SARLs; minimum net wealth tax is €535 (balance-sheet total ≤ €350,000) or €3,210 (balance-sheet total > €350,000 or financial-assets test met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment triggers an enforceable collection order and late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; persistent non-filing may be fined up to €25,000 under the General Tax Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RBE annual confirmation of beneficial owners (Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE online platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 30 days of the LBR annual confirmation reminder, anchored to the anniversary of the initial RBE filing; any change in the ownership chain must be re-filed within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from €250 to €2,000 under the amended law of 13 January 2019; for intentional omissions, criminal fines up to €1,250 per director and up to €10,000 for the legal entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered-office continuance and establishment permit conformity (autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual renewal; the commercial establishment permit and registered-office arrangement remain valid indefinitely, but any change of gérant, registered office, or business scope must be declared within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare qualifying changes may lead to the withdrawal of the establishment permit and, in repeated or serious cases, fines up to €10,000 or judicial strike-off proceedings; for ISIC 4661 commodity brokerage, compliance with the permit registers is a precondition for maintaining SPE/trading counterparty status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé is mandatory for a Luxembourg SARL exceeding two of the three small-company exemptions in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total > €4.4 million, net turnover > €8.8 million, average headcount > 50; audit is also compulsory where the SARL is consolidated into a group required to file audited accounts, or where sectoral energy-commodity licensing conditions impose an auditor's report.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 and the amended Règlement grand-ducal implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for statutory annual accounts of non-listed commercial companies; commodity inventory must be valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value; accounts are presented in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ownership data must be filed in the RBE within 30 days of any change in the shareholding or control chain, and a statutory annual confirmation of the correctness of the RBE filing must be completed online through the LBR/MyGuichet workflow within 30 days of each annual reminder; the gérant must re-collect KYC packs, corporate organigrams, transfer deeds and control-chain evidence before attesting; for the ISIC 4661 high-risk wholesale fuel segment, exact percentages, direct/indirect control and material influence must be reported for each UBO.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des parts sociales) with quantitative holdings and endorsement of each transfer
Register of Directors (registre des gérants and administrative resolutions)
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings
Register of Bank Loans and encumbrances (registre des prêts bancaires)
UBO due-diligence file reproducing the RBE declaration and supporting control-chart evidence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – USD 12,000 per year for a professional fiduciary, registered office and company-secretarial scope for a commodity-brokerage SARL
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 – USD 45,000 per year for a typical non-listed SARL in the physical fuel and distillate brokerage segment with moderate transaction volumes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax (IRC) for taxable income above EUR 175,000; 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 175,000 (art. 174 LIR). After 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC and 6.75% municipal business tax for Luxembourg City, the top aggregate effective rate is 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for SARLs in Luxembourg. Preferential mechanisms: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend income (art. 166 LIR) and capital gains (art. 167 LIR) where holding is >=10% or acquisition cost >= EUR 1.2 million and, for gains, a 12-month holding period is satisfied; Luxembourg group relief (integration fiscale) for >=95%-owned subsidiaries; IP box regime grandfathered for assets acquired before 30 June 2021 (expiring 30 June 2024); investment tax credit up to 12% for eligible digital and tangible assets; ATAD interest limitation rule (30% EBITDA) applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry); annual offset capped at 70% of taxable income exceeding EUR 200,000 (art. 110 LIR)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modèle 542 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune). Electronic filing via eCDF portal (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) using a valid LuxTrust certificate; alternatively, paper filing at the competent bureau d'imposition.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end where the fiscal year equals the calendar year. Extension to 31 December is routinely granted upon request. Corporate income tax prepayments are due quarterly on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December; any residual balance is due upon final assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address, Luxembourg business registration number (RCS), legal form (SARL), ISIC/NACE 4661 code, fiscal year dates and competent tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not required to appear on the SARL's return; only a Luxembourg permanent establishment attributable activity of a non-resident is reported here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A.2 - Directors and authorised signatories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of managers (gérants), directors, and statutory auditors; identity, nationality and residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident directors; this is a key economic substance indicator for tax residence and treaty access.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net trading result from wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates per audited statutory accounts: gross margin, commissions, trading fees, hedging results and other operating income minus operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-source and PE-attributable trading income is taxable; foreign trading income booked offshore without a Luxembourg PE must not be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back of non-deductible items: fines, penalties, excessive interest, excessive management remuneration, 50% of entertainment expenses, and excess portion of intercompany financing costs under the ATAD EBITDA cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same adjustments apply to a Luxembourg PE of a non-resident; treaty-protected foreign taxes on income excluded from Luxembourg tax base are added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividends under art. 166 LIR and exempt capital gains under art. 167 LIR from strategic holdings in crude oil logistics, storage or trading affiliates meeting the holding threshold and the subject-to-tax condition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach evidence of taxation of the distributing subsidiary, holding period computation and TRC; non-resident PEs enjoy the same participation exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses offset against current taxable income, subject to the 70% cap on income exceeding EUR 200,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a non-resident's foreign PE cannot be offset in Luxembourg unless the treaty assigns taxing rights to Luxembourg and the PE is effectively connected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D.200 - Municipal business tax and net wealth tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable capital for net wealth tax (equity plus long-term liabilities minus qualifying participations) and municipal business tax base; Luxembourg City ICC rate 6.75% (2024).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE computes its own ICC base in the commune of the PE; NWT applies to the net assets employed in the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions: commodity purchase/sale margins, brokering fees, stand-by letter of credit (SBLC) and working capital financing charges, guarantee fees and cost contribution arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related parties must support pricing under OECD TP; attach Local File when the Luxembourg entity's turnover is >= EUR 1 million and group turnover is >= EUR 50 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; for minor delay, commonly a penalty of EUR 1,000 to EUR 1,500 plus a 10% increase of assessed tax; default assessment may raise tax due by up to 100% where concealment is found. Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum). Willful failure to file exposes directors to criminal proceedings and personal liability for corporate tax debts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (art. 90 LIR). Reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate shareholder holds >=10% for at least 12 months; many Luxembourg tax treaties reduce the rate to 5% or 10% for portfolio holdings and 0% for qualifying substantial holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the residence state, submit Form 105 (application for exemption or reduction of Luxembourg dividend withholding tax) to the competent ACD office, and provide shareholder registers demonstrating the qualifying holding period. The Luxembourg paying agent may apply the reduced rate only upon receipt of valid self-certification and TRC; otherwise the 15% statutory rate is withheld and the shareholder must claim reimbursement from the ACD within five years. For outbound royalties and interest, no WHT applies at source, so no treaty relief protocol is generally required; however, the payer must maintain documentary evidence of arm's length character and beneficial ownership to pre-empt anti-abuse recharacterisation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound royalties under domestic law, mirrored in Luxembourg tax treaties (no royalty WHT). Interest: 0% statutory WHT on outbound interest on arm's length debt; anti-abuse recharacterisation applies to back-to-back or artificial financing arrangements under Circular L.G.-A n° 62 of 15 January 2018. Commodity trade finance costs, SBLC commission and discount charges must be at arm's length and documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File: required where the consolidated group revenue is >= EUR 50 million. Local File: required where the Luxembourg entity's annual net turnover is >= EUR 1 million and group consolidated revenue is >= EUR 50 million (Circular 2017/1); CbCR: required for groups with consolidated revenue >= EUR 750 million. All amounts in EUR.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to UAE-style regimes; however, substantive minimum-threshold tests are mandatory through: (i) the General Anti-Abuse Rule (art. 6 LIR and paragraph 6 of the Luxembourg Tax Adaptation Act); (ii) TP functional and risk analysis under Circulars 2017/1-2017/4; (iii) the participation exemption conditions (subject-to-tax and, for capital gains, 12-month holding); (iv) beneficial-ownership analysis for treaty and EU Directive claims; and (v) for a marine fuel oil and distillates trading SARL: a physical trading desk in Luxembourg, local risk-management and decision-making staff, independent office premises, bank accounts and capitalisation sufficient for the trading volume, and documented trade transactions, failing which profits may be re-attributed to the real principal jurisdiction and treaty benefits denied under the MLI principal purpose test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate false declaration of crude oil and refined product trading profits, fabrication of invoices from shell suppliers, concealment of offshore brokerage accounts, or fraudulent offset of non-existent losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to EUR 500,000 under the Criminal Code and art. 396-1 LIR; reassessment of the full tax shortfall plus 0.6% monthly interest; civil surcharge of up to 100% of the evaded tax; publication of the conviction; in aggravated cases, asset freezing and confiscation of trading proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be held jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts where they knowingly signed false returns; exposure to criminal penalties, travel bans, personal asset seizure and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Luxembourg SARL booking trading profits without real staff, premises or decision-making authority; all purchase and resale decisions made abroad; no commercial rationale for the Luxembourg entity; profits merely pass through with immediate dividend distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the Luxembourg entity for tax purposes, re-attribution of profits to the foreign principal, denial of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test, recharacterisation of contracts, retroactive reassessment with 100% surcharge and interest, mandatory DAC6 disclosure penalties up to EUR 250,000, and removal from the Luxembourg commercial register in extreme cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability to the tax authority for the full corporate tax debt upon veil-piercing; administrative fines; disqualification from office; in cross-border fraud cases, extradition exposure and personal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Settling oil trades through third-party shell SPVs, handling proceeds for sanctioned suppliers (Iran, Venezuela, Russia), using cash or precious metals for settlement, falsifying bills of lading and brokerage invoices to launder funds, or failing to identify ultimate beneficial owners as required for the wholesale licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004: fines up to EUR 5,000,000 for legal persons and imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering (Criminal Code art. 506-1); confiscation of assets and trading proceeds; revocation of the mandatory wholesale licence; CSSF administrative sanctions and delisting from trade finance facilities; freezing orders under EU sanctions regulations; exclusion from SBLC and SWIFT-based payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability of up to 10 years imprisonment, personal confiscation of funds, travel bans, professional debarment, and potential OFAC secondary sanctions exposure for USD clearing; corporate veil may be pierced to recover laundered proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length mark-ups on wholesale marine fuel and distillates, artificial hub-invoicing to book profit in Luxembourg or in a zero-tax jurisdiction, off-market SBLC fees, round-trip trades to inflate margins, or undocumented intercompany commodity financing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment by the ACD plus secondary adjustment and 0.6% monthly interest; penalty of 25% of the additional tax for gross negligence; documentation penalty up to EUR 25,000 for failure to produce Local/Master File; extended 10-year assessment limitation period where the taxpayer has not declared cross-border related-party transactions; EU Arbitration Directive mutual agreement procedure where no relief is obtained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structured or approved the mispricing may be personally liable for the additional tax where the arrangement lacks commercial substance; risk of criminal proceedings for tax fraud in intentional cases, travel restrictions, and claw-back claims by minority shareholders or liquidators.
